item.text: I’m using the executable as a bytes-format oracle for the tricky part now: Python doesn’t just dump raw bytes, it prints a `repr(bytes)` string with Python’s quoting and escape rules. That output has to be matched exactly, so I’m probing those rules before I finalize the formatter.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "shell_quote() {
  printf '%q' \""'$1"
}
probe() {
  label=$1
  value=$2
  out1="/tmp/probe_${label}_1_$$.out"
  err1="/tmp/probe_${label}_1_$$.err"
  out2="/tmp/probe_${label}_2_$$.out"
  err2="/tmp/probe_${label}_2_$$.err"
  set +e
  /workspace/dataset/test7_executable --a "$value" --b 2g >"$out1" 2>"$err1"
  code1=$?
  set -e
  printf '"'CASE=%s input=%s\\nencode_exit=%s\\nencode_stdout<<\\n' \""'$label" "$(shell_quote "$value")" "$code1"
  cat "$out1"
  printf '"'\\nencode_stderr<<\\n'
  cat \""'$err1"
  if [ "$code1" -eq 0 ]; then
    encoded=$(head -n 1 "$out1" | sed -e "s/''^b'"'//\" -e \"s/'"'$//")
    set +e
    /workspace/dataset/test7_executable --a x --b "$encoded" >"$out2" 2>"$err2"
    code2=$?

    printf '"'\\ndecode_arg=%s\\ndecode_exit=%s\\ndecode_stdout<<\\n' \""'$encoded" "$code2"
    cat "$out2"
    printf '"'\\ndecode_stderr<<\\n'
    cat \""'$err2"
  fi
  printf '"'\\nENDCASE\\n'
}
